ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure has a circle inscribed in a square, and the circle is tangent to the square's upper, lower, left, and right four sides respectively. Beside the right side of the square, a length of 32 is labeled, and there are right-angle marks at the four corners. Reasoning: The diameter of a circle inscribed in a square equals the side length of the square. Therefore the diameter of the circle d = 32. The circumference formula for a circle is C = πd, so C = π × 32 = 32π.

The right side of the square is labeled 32, so the square's side length is 32. Since an inscribed circle in a square has diameter equal to the square's side length, the circle's diameter is 32. Use the circumference formula C = πd to get C = 32π.
